work.permit: child performance licence granted by the local authority

note: Read 2026-10-31 on legislation.gov.uk (revised texts). Majority: Family Law Reform Act 1969, s.1 (England and Wales): a person attains full age at eighteen; Northern Ireland's Age of Majority Act (Northern Ireland) 1969 sets the same eighteen (not read today; NI isn't a region of its own here since it matches). Scotland: Age of Legal Capacity (Scotland) Act 1991, s.1: a person of or over sixteen has legal capacity to enter into any transaction, under sixteen none (s.2's exceptions for transactions common for a person of that age aren't held); GB.SCT is 16 because the form's majority is the age of contracting in one's own name. Not held: s.3 of the 1991 Act, by which a person under twenty-one may ask a court to set aside a prejudicial transaction made at sixteen or seventeen; Scotland's age of majority for other purposes stays eighteen (Age of Majority (Scotland) Act 1969, not read). Work: Children and Young Persons Act 1933, s.18(1)(a) (England and Wales): no child may be employed under fourteen (local byelaws may let a child of thirteen do light work, not held); Education Act 1996, s.558: for the laws on employment of children, anyone not over compulsory school age is a child; s.8(3): compulsory school age ends on the school leaving date of the year a person turns sixteen (the last Friday in June in England, set by order). The form's 16 is that leaving age, the first age at which a person is no longer a 'child' under these laws; England's duty to stay in education or training to eighteen (Education and Skills Act 2008) allows work beside part-time training and isn't held. Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own like rules (Children and Young Persons (Scotland) Act 1937; not read). Performers: Children and Young Persons Act 1963, s.37 (England, Wales and Scotland): a child may not take part in a paid or broadcast performance, or model or do paid sport, except under a licence granted by the local authority where the child lives; the licence has no lowest age in the Act (the Children (Performances and Activities) Regulations 2014 set its conditions, not read). Service: none. The PA Media report carried by BreakingNews.ie (26 May 2024, marked secondary) states that compulsory national service, for fit men of eighteen to twenty-six, was abolished in 1960. The United Kingdom has no conscription in force (the National Service Act 1948's call-up ended in 1960); the armed forces recruit volunteers.

sources.title: Family Law Reform Act 1969, section 1 (legislation.gov.uk)
sources.said: a person shall attain full age on attaining the age of eighteen instead of on attaining the age of twenty-one

sources.title: Age of Legal Capacity (Scotland) Act 1991, section 1 (legislation.gov.uk)
sources.said: a person under the age of 16 years shall, subject to section 2 below, have no legal capacity to enter into any transaction; ... a person of or over the age of 16 years shall have legal capacity to enter into any transaction.

sources.title: Children and Young Persons Act 1933, section 18 (legislation.gov.uk)
sources.said: Restrictions on employment of children. ... no child shall be employed

sources.title: Education Act 1996, section 558 (legislation.gov.uk)
sources.said: For the purposes of any enactment relating to the prohibition or regulation of the employment of children or young persons, any person who is not over compulsory school age shall be deemed to be a child within the meaning of that enactment.

sources.title: Education Act 1996, section 8 (legislation.gov.uk)
sources.said: A person ceases to be of compulsory school age at the end of the day which is the school leaving date for any calendar year— ... if he attains the age of 16 after that day but before the beginning of the school year next following,

sources.title: Children and Young Persons Act 1963, section 37 (legislation.gov.uk)
sources.said: Restriction on persons under 16 taking part in public performances, ... except under the authority of a licence granted by the local authority in whose area he resides

sources.title: BreakingNews.ie (PA Media), "What was national service and how does it work in other countries?", 26 May 2024
sources.said: The most recent form of compulsory national service, which required all physically fit male British citizens aged between 18 and 26 to serve in the armed forces, was abolished in 1960.
